stem: A 71-year-old man with severe knee osteoarthritis takes ibuprofen daily. Four months ago a bleeding gastric ulcer healed with treatment, and tests for Helicobacter pylori were negative. He refuses to stop the ibuprofen and has no other medical problems.
oneliner: 71M + knee osteoarthritis on daily ibuprofen + healed bleeding gastric ulcer + H. pylori negative + will not stop ibuprofen → which drug prevents recurrence by replacing what ibuprofen removes?
ask: Which of the following drugs best targets the cause of his ulcer while he continues the ibuprofen?

whyNot.A: **Coats the ulcer base**; does not replace prostaglandins or prevent NSAID ulcers
whyNot.C: **Coating agent** for H. pylori regimens; he is H. pylori negative
whyNot.E: **Antacid**; neutralizes acid but does not restore mucosal defenses

why: **NSAIDs block COX-1**, so the stomach loses protective prostaglandins (less mucus and bicarbonate, more acid). **Misoprostol is a PGE1 analog** that restores this protection.

drug.name: Misoprostol
drug.how: Activates EP receptors on parietal and mucous cells: less acid, more mucus and bicarbonate
drug.use: Prevention of NSAID-induced gastric ulcers; medical abortion with mifepristone; postpartum hemorrhage
drug.watch: Diarrhea, abdominal cramps; contraindicated in pregnancy (uterine contractions)

chain: Acid falls, mucus and bicarbonate rise

stem: A 45-year-old woman has had burning behind the breastbone after meals for 2 years. She raised the head of her bed and stopped late meals, but nothing helped. Endoscopy shows linear erosions in the distal esophagus with no Barrett metaplasia. She wants the drug that will heal the erosions most reliably.
oneliner: 45F + 2 y postprandial heartburn + no response to lifestyle changes + linear distal esophageal erosions → which drug heals them best?
ask: Which of the following drugs is most appropriate?

whyNot.A: **H2 blocker**: weaker acid suppression; heals erosions less reliably
whyNot.B: **Prokinetic**: little effect on acid, and brings neurologic side effects
whyNot.C: **Prostaglandin analog**: used for NSAID ulcers; causes diarrhea
whyNot.E: **Muscarinic agonist**: raises acid secretion and can worsen reflux

why: **Erosive esophagitis unresponsive to lifestyle change** needs the strongest acid suppression. A **PPI such as omeprazole** heals esophageal mucosa better than an H2 blocker.

drug.name: Omeprazole
drug.how: Irreversibly inhibits the H+/K+ ATPase of parietal cells
drug.use: GERD, erosive esophagitis, peptic ulcers, H. pylori regimens, Zollinger-Ellison
drug.watch: Long-term: C. difficile, pneumonia, hypomagnesemia, low B12, fractures, interstitial nephritis; reduces absorption of drugs needing acid

stem: An 18-month-old boy has had 2 days of frequent watery stools. He is irritable but still drinks eagerly. His mucous membranes are dry, his eyes are mildly sunken, and skin tents briefly. He has no blood in the stool and no vomiting.
oneliner: 18-mo boy + 2 d watery diarrhea + dry mucosa, mildly sunken eyes, drinks eagerly + no vomiting → which fluid?
ask: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.C: Oral solution of glucose and sodium

whyNot.A: **No glucose**: sodium is not absorbed efficiently
whyNot.B: **Sugar-rich, low sodium**: draws water into the gut and worsens diarrhea

why: **Mild to moderate dehydration in a child who can drink** is treated by mouth. **Glucose and sodium are absorbed together** (SGLT1) and water follows, even during diarrhea.

drug.name: Oral rehydration solution
drug.how: Glucose and Na+ are cotransported by SGLT1; water follows
drug.use: Dehydration from acute diarrhea, including cholera
drug.watch: Hypernatremia if mixed too concentrated; not for severe shock or persistent vomiting

stem: A 48-year-old man has fainted twice. He has had 5 L a day of watery diarrhea for 3 months, and it continues when he fasts. He has facial flushing and cramps. Serum potassium is 2.6 mEq/L, bicarbonate is 17 mEq/L, and gastric acid output is low. CT shows a 4-cm mass in the pancreatic tail, and vasoactive intestinal peptide is 600 pg/mL. He awaits surgery.
oneliner: 48M + fainting + 5 L/day watery diarrhea persisting on fasting + flushing + K 2.6, HCO3 17 + low gastric acid + 4-cm pancreatic tail mass + VIP 600 → which drug controls diarrhea until surgery?
ask: Which of the following drugs is most appropriate?

whyNot.A: **Opioid**: too weak against this secretory volume
whyNot.B: **Bile acid binder**: treats bile acid diarrhea, not hormone-driven secretion
whyNot.D: **PPI**: his acid output is already low; the diarrhea is not acid-driven

why: **Watery diarrhea that persists with fasting + hypokalemia + achlorhydria + pancreatic mass + high VIP** = VIPoma. **Octreotide is a somatostatin analog** that inhibits the tumor's hormone release and intestinal secretion.

drug.name: Octreotide
drug.how: Activates somatostatin receptors: less hormone release (VIP, GH, insulin, glucagon) and less intestinal secretion
drug.use: VIPoma, carcinoid, acromegaly, variceal bleeding, secretory diarrhea
drug.watch: Gallstones, steatorrhea, bradycardia, hyper- or hypoglycemia

chain: VIP release and gut secretion fall

stem: A 59-year-old woman with lung cancer is about to receive cisplatin. She wants medication started before the infusion to prevent nausea and vomiting.
oneliner: 59F + lung cancer + about to start cisplatin + wants prophylaxis against nausea → which drug?
ask: Which of the following is the most effective drug to give before the infusion?

whyNot.B: **D2 blocker / prokinetic**: less effective for cisplatin; can cause dystonia
whyNot.C: **D2 blocker**: weaker, causes sedation and extrapyramidal effects
whyNot.D: **Cannabinoid**: reserved for refractory nausea; sedation and dysphoria
whyNot.E: **Antimuscarinic patch**: for motion sickness, not chemotherapy

why: **Cisplatin is highly emetogenic** and triggers serotonin release from gut cells. A **5-HT3 antagonist such as ondansetron** is the best prophylaxis among these options.

drug.name: Ondansetron
drug.how: Blocks 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents and in the chemoreceptor trigger zone
drug.use: Chemotherapy, radiation and postoperative nausea and vomiting
drug.watch: Headache, constipation, QT prolongation, serotonin syndrome (rare)

stem: A 54-year-old man with 20 years of heavy alcohol use has lost 8 kg over 6 months. He passes bulky, greasy, foul-smelling stools that float. CT shows calcifications in the pancreas, and fecal elastase is 60 mcg/g (normal above 200). He has no abdominal pain at present.
oneliner: 54M + 20 y heavy alcohol + 8-kg weight loss + greasy floating stools + pancreatic calcifications + fecal elastase 60 → which drug?
ask: Which of the following is most appropriate?

whyNot.A: **Opioid**: slows stool but does not fix fat digestion
whyNot.C: **Somatostatin analog**: reduces secretions and worsens fat absorption

why: **Chronic pancreatitis + steatorrhea + low fecal elastase** = pancreatic exocrine insufficiency. **Pancrelipase** supplies lipase, protease and amylase with meals.

drug.name: Pancrelipase
drug.how: Supplies lipase, protease and amylase to digest fat, protein and starch
drug.use: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis)
drug.watch: Take with meals; fibrosing colonopathy at very high doses; abdominal cramps
